name: Historical Park (Temple Island Core)
description: The heart of Ayutthaya on the river island, where the UNESCO Historical Park spreads its brick temples and prangs. Wat Mahathat, Wat Phra Si Sanphet and shaded lanes make this the atmospheric, culturally rich core to base near.
bestFor: Culture lovers and cyclists who want ruins and heritage on their doorstep
pros: Extraordinary temples within walking or cycling distance
Quiet, calm evenings near the monuments

name: Naresuan Road / Soi Farang
tagline: Backpacker hub of guesthouses and cafes
description: The traveller strip around Naresuan Road and Soi Farang, packed with guesthouses, hostels, cafes, bike hire and relaxed bars. It is the most social, English-friendly pocket and the easiest landing spot for short-stay nomads and backpackers.
bestFor: Backpackers and short-stay nomads wanting cafes, bikes and easy company
pros: Most cafes, wifi and bike rental
Central and walkable to the ruins
cons: Can feel touristy and a bit worn

name: Riverside and Floating Market Area
description: The riverbanks and floating-market area ringing the island, where restaurants, boat trips and evening markets line the water. Sunset views over riverside temples like Wat Chaiwatthanaram make this the most scenic, laid-back place to eat and unwind.
bestFor: Slow travellers who love river views, boat trips and evening market food
pros: Beautiful river and sunset temple views
cons: Spread out and quieter for daily errands

name: Modern Town Toward the Station
description: The modern district across the river toward the railway station, where locals live, shop and eat. Markets, shops, transport links and cheaper long-stay rooms make it practical and authentic, trading temple atmosphere for daily convenience and value.
bestFor: Budget long-stayers wanting local prices, markets and easy train connections
pros: Right by the station for Bangkok trips
cons: Less English and fewer tourist cafes
